name: cmathl
listed_description: Math library with a great variety of mathematical functions with CMake build support. Seeks to be close to C89/C90 compliant for portability.
reason: Archived by the owner on 2022-10-10 (57 stars, MIT). README and CHANGELOG contain no benchmark, speed or libm/glibc comparison; the only accuracy statement is that unit tests check functions against CML_FLT_EPSILON and CML_DBL_EPSILON. The project site (scientificc.github.io/cmathl) is blocked in this environment.

name: Cuba
reason: feynarts.de, arxiv.org and ar5iv were unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) and no GitHub mirror of the C library was found. Search snippets show Hahn's papers (hep-ph/0404043, hep-ph/0509016) compare only Cuba's own four algorithms (Vegas, Suave, Divonne, Cuhre; Fig. 1 on an e+e- phase-space integral) and mention no external baseline numbers (GSL, NAG, CUBPACK). No third-party shootout including Cuba as the faster library was reachable.

name: d-SEAMS
listed_description: A molecular dynamics trajectory analysis engine in C++ and Lua with Nix. It is an acronym for Deferred Structural Elucidation Analysis for Molecular Simulations.
reason: seams-core README has no speed claims. The linked reproducibility package (https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams2_repro, MIT, results/reference/elja-1798666, AMD EPYC 7713, meson release, bench code g++ -std=c++20 -O2) times only the 2.0 engine against its own pre-2.0 release (seams-base 1c8efa3): 32000 atoms ringNetwork 5111.481 ms to 752.863 ms, byIndex 8689.630 ms to 59.256 ms, neighListO 862.833 ms to 60.985 ms; 4096-atom findHC 4926.91 ms vs 68.655 ms. That is a self-comparison against an earlier version, not an outside baseline. The only external-tool sweep (sota_compare.txt, 360-512 molecule lattices) reports accuracy and shows freud (median 9-11 ms) and CHILL+ (3-4 ms) faster than d-SEAMS topology classifiers (23-46 ms), and OVITO PTM failed to import (libxkbcommon.so.0 missing). Lead for the orchestrator if self-version comparisons are ever wanted: dseams2_repro tip vs base numbers above.

name: darknet
listed_description: Open source neural network framework written in C and CUDA.
reason: README at HEAD carries only model-level FPS tables for YOLOv7 (PyTorch repo WongKinYiu/yolov7) against YOLOv5, YOLOX, SWIN-L, ConvNeXt and others, not the Darknet framework against TensorFlow or PyTorch. YOLOv3 paper figures seen in search snippets (51 ms vs RetinaNet 198 ms on a Titan X) are also model comparisons. pjreddie.com is unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND, arxiv.org too); three searches found no framework-level number (Orpheus paper only scores DarkNet qualitatively; CIANNA benchmarks CIANNA against TF and PyTorch, not Darknet).

name: Fido
listed_description: A highly-modular C++ machine learning library for embedded electronics and robotics.
reason: MIT, 464 stars, beta status. README and repo page contain no benchmark, speed or comparison claim (only 'lightweight' and minimal standard-library use); a search for Fido benchmarks against TensorFlow, Caffe or tiny-dnn returned nothing. Project site fidoproject.github.io is blocked here.

name: ggml
listed_description: Tensor library for machine learning with 16-bit and 4-bit quantization support.
reason: Repo moved to https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml (MIT, 15.5k stars, active; last commit seen 2026-10-05). README has no numbers. Example READMEs give absolute timings only (gpt-2 117M 5 ms/token, gpt-j 124.62 ms/token on an M1 Pro, mnist 7.69 us/image) with no baseline. llama.cpp PR #6414 (tinyBLAS, now in ggml-cpu) compares only against prior llama.cpp HEAD (F16 prompt 13 to 52 tok/s on an i9-14900K), not MKL or PyTorch. stable-diffusion.cpp issue #248 shows the opposite on CPU (about 5 s per step vs 1.43 s for diffusers after -O3). Third-party threads (Hugging Face forum, mpt-7b discussion) and the llamafile matmul blog are blocked and snippets carry no numbers.
